models.architecture: Conformer RNNT, 120M parameters, striding 4x, Catalan and Spanish
models.attribution: stt_ca-es_conformer_transducer_large by the Language Technologies Unit of the Barcelona Supercomputing Center (Abir Messaoudi, Baybars Külebi), Projecte Aina, funded by ILENIA. https://huggingface.co/projecte-aina/stt_ca-es_conformer_transducer_large

conversion.command: convert_model.py stt_ca-es_conformer_transducer_large.nemo --architecture asr --head-type rnnt --outtype q8_0 --no-embed-pe -o catalan-conformer-q8.gguf
conversion.notes: The mel filterbank is copied from the checkpoint. The positional-encoding table is omitted and rebuilt by the runtime at load time (20 MB smaller file, identical transcripts). The output is deterministic: two conversions give the same SHA-256.

evaluation.corpus: FLEURS ca_es test, first 45 utterances, plus the owner's three recordings (reading, free speech, noise) cut into 29 fragments of 8 s: 1665 words.
results: Parity with an independent reference (OpenVoiceOS FP32 ONNX export run with onnx-asr): 72 of 74 fragments identical, 6 of 1665 words differ. In the one substantive difference our engine is right ('l'any mil nou-cents noranta-dos', as read).
Runtime-built positional table against the embedded one, F16: all 74 transcripts identical.

Compression against F16: Q8_0 2 words differ (foreign fragments); Q6_K 2 differ, one an inserted Spanish 'vale'; Q5_K 7 differ; Q4_K 23 differ, including errors on the owner's voice. Q8_0 is the smallest variant without a measurable regression.

Live pipeline, owner voice, Reliable profile, fixed clock. Reading (214 words): 4 s 4.7% WER, 6 s 2.3%, 8 s 2.3%; noise (60 words): 4 s 5.0%, 6 s 3.3%. The model sometimes drops the apostrophe of elisions ('l acordió'); CatalanElisionRepair restores it.

Live window chosen on 2026-09-25 with 87 ParlamentParla v3 clips (4,296 words of spontaneous speech, fixed clock, Reliable profile): WER 6 s 15.3%, 7 s 15.0%, 8 s 14.7%; stable-text latency P95 on the owner's reading 1.13, 1.10 and 1.24 s (8 s is over the Reliable 1.2 s target). 7 s is the live setting. The model card lists ParlamentParla v3 among its training data, so these clips measure the window, not the model.

Chosen as the app's only model on 2026-09-26 after a comparison with the former default (BSC Catalan Parakeet RNNT 1.1B, Q4_K, 4 s window) on audio neither had been trained on (.work/clean-test): FLEURS ca test, 150 read sentences, 3.8% WER against 4.0%; 60 EMpodcat conversation clips, 12.8% against 14.6% (clip edges excluded; 95% interval of the gap 0.8 to 2.8 points); two full Softcatalà podcast episodes (35 min, 3-6 voices), 7.3% against 8.5%. Spanish words in Catalan speech: 1 against 3. Also decided on licence (CC-BY-4.0), size (131 MB against 612 MB) and fit on iPhone.
evaluation.notes: Replacing the checkpoint requires a reproducible corpus the candidate was not trained on (.work/clean-test is one), a lower WER in conversation, no more Spanish words, fewer non-speech insertions, and no material latency regression. Any new compression must show no measurable regression against the F16 conversion on the same audio.

models.architecture: FastConformer hybrid RNNT+CTC (RNNT head), 114M parameters, dw_striding 8x, Spanish, writes punctuation and capitals

conversion.command: convert_model.py stt_es_fastconformer_hybrid_large_pc.nemo --architecture asr --head-type rnnt --outtype q8_0 --no-embed-pe -o spanish-fastconformer-q8.gguf
conversion.notes: The auxiliary CTC head of the hybrid checkpoint (0.53 M parameters, unused by the RNNT decoder) is skipped by a one-line converter change (.work/lang-spike/tools/converter-copy/ctc_skip.patch); 60/60 transcripts are identical with and without it.

evaluation.corpus: FLEURS es_419 test (Google, CC-BY-4.0), first 60 and 150 utterances of 3-15 s, read speech; .work/lang-spike
results: Offline: 4.13% WER (n=150), 4.27% (n=60); Q8_0 against F16: 59/60 identical.
Live pipeline (7 s window, fixed clock), after the seam-repeat fix of 2026-09-28: 4.72% WER (n=60), was 6.45% with 20 repeated words at window seams.
Punctuation as shown to the reader (RecognizerPunctuation + TranscriptFormatter): sentence end F1 0.91, comma F1 0.76, questions 1.0, capitals 98%.

models.architecture: FastConformer hybrid RNNT+CTC (RNNT head), 114M parameters, dw_striding 8x, English, writes punctuation and capitals

conversion.command: convert_model.py stt_en_fastconformer_hybrid_large_pc.nemo --architecture asr --head-type rnnt --outtype q8_0 --no-embed-pe -o english-fastconformer-q8.gguf
conversion.notes: The auxiliary CTC head of the hybrid checkpoint (0.53 M parameters, unused by the RNNT decoder) is skipped by a one-line converter change (.work/lang-spike/tools/converter-copy/ctc_skip.patch); 60/60 transcripts are identical with and without it.

evaluation.corpus: FLEURS en_us test (Google, CC-BY-4.0), 60 utterances of 3-15 s; .work/lang-spike
results: Offline: 4.68% WER (n=60), about 4.0% with spelling variants forgiven.
Live pipeline after the seam-repeat fix of 2026-09-28: 5.59% WER, was 7.72% with 22 repeated words at window seams.

models.architecture: Conformer RNNT, 120M parameters, striding 4x, Catalan, Spanish, Galician and Basque, writes punctuation and capitals
models.attribution: stt_los_conformer_transducer_large_punctuated by the Language Technologies Unit of the Barcelona Supercomputing Center (Abir Messaoudi, Sarah Solito, Carlos Hernández Mena, Cristina España-Bonet). https://huggingface.co/BSC-LT/stt_los_conformer_transducer_large_punctuated

conversion.notes: Stock converter with the local striding patch.

evaluation.corpus: FLEURS gl_es test (Google, CC-BY-4.0), 60 utterances; the model card lists FLEURS Galician among its training data without naming splits, so read the numbers as optimistic
results: Offline: 7.58% WER (the unpunctuated LoS model: 7.73%); sentence end precision 1.00, recall 0.69; comma F1 0.78; capitals 98%.
Slips into Spanish word forms in about 0.5% of words (ceremonia, fue, decir); the model takes no language prompt.

models.architecture: Conformer RNNT, 120M parameters, striding 4x, Basque, lowercase without punctuation
models.attribution: stt_eu_conformer_transducer_large_v2 by HiTZ (Basque Center for Language Technology, UPV/EHU). https://huggingface.co/HiTZ/stt_eu_conformer_transducer_large_v2

conversion.command: convert_model.py stt_eu_conformer_transducer_large_v2.nemo --architecture asr --head-type rnnt --outtype q8_0 --no-embed-pe -o basque-conformer-q8.gguf
conversion.notes: Stock converter with the local striding patch.

evaluation.corpus: HiTZ composite_corpus_eu_v2.1 test_parl (Basque Parliament, 60) and test_oslr (OpenSLR 76, 50); .work/lang-spike
results: Offline: 3.19% WER on Parliament, 12.33% on OpenSLR; the punctuated BSC LoS model scored 4.92% and 16.44% on the same clips (without clips where it writes digits), so Basque keeps this recogniser and gets its own punctuation model.

punctuation.model: Our Catalan punctuation and capitalisation model v3: v2 (projecte-aina/distilroberta-base-ca-v2, Apache-2.0, fine-tuned on Common Voice CA sentences and CATalog parliamentary transcripts, all CC0) trained a further 105 min on 8.3M words of CC0 parliamentary transcripts plus Common Voice, 60% of examples cropped to random windows so it decides well with the three words of right context the app gives it. Core ML, 6-bit palettised, 59 MB.
punctuation.labels: 24 labels, <mark><case>: marks none , . ? ! :, cases l u e a.
evaluation: Live, as the app uses it (32 words before, 3 after), F1: FLEURS sentence end 78 (v2 69), comma 62; Softcatalà podcasts sentence end 54 (v2 38), comma 64, question 38 (v2 28), sentence-start capital 71 (v2 56).
Full context, F1: FLEURS sentence end 83, comma 65, proper nouns 73; podcasts sentence end 56, comma 65, question 52. The 6-bit Core ML model scores within one point of PyTorch.
Training paragraphs sharing any 8-word sequence with FLEURS, the podcasts, the founder's recordings or the ParlamentParla calibration clips were removed (36 paragraphs).
Swift port against Python on 2026-09-25: tokenizer identical on 24,921 words; labels identical on 37,254 words (336 paragraphs); number normalisation identical on 4,354 lines.
Live pipeline: a few ms per update; words freeze with three words of right context, or when the speaker pauses.

speakers.model: pyannote segmentation-3.0 (MIT, CNRS; weights from onnx-community/pyannote-segmentation-3.0 at 733a93b6, ONNX SHA-256 057ee564…ea25), rebuilt in PyTorch and converted to Core ML float32 by scripts/convert-speaker-model.py. 1.5M parameters, 5.7 MB. Hears voices, not words: the same model serves every language.
evaluation: Core ML against ONNX Runtime on a 15-minute podcast (Softcatalà, 3-6 voices): 53,010 of 53,010 frames give the same class; largest logit difference 0.0003.

packMirror.notes: languages[].mirror: the .aar written by stage-ios-resources.sh --asset-packs (the file uploaded to App Store Connect), published as a GitHub release asset. The app fetches it only when the App Store's pack fails or stalls, verifies the SHA-256 of the whole archive, then unpacks Contents/<id>. Neither app bundles a language (BUNDLED_LANGUAGES is empty); a bundled one would never download. Re-run --asset-packs, then update sha256 and bytes here and upload the new .aar to the release, whenever a pack changes.
